source.title: Explicit Eigenvalue Regularization Improves Sharpness-Aware Minimization
source.authors: Hao-Cheng Luo; Tuan Truong; Tung Pham; Mehrtash Harandi; Dinh Q. Phung; Trung Le

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares sharpness-aware training methods and measures test accuracy and Hessian sharpness, bearing on whether a sharpness measure tracks generalization. It does not use the magnitude-aware perturbation measure named in V7.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-accuracy comparisons among SGD, SAM, and Eigen-SAM and a qualitative Hessian-spectrum comparison. These results concern sharpness and test performance but do not test any listed version's specific intervention or measure. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a sharpness–generalization rationale to develop Eigen-SAM and reports its performance. It tests none of V1–V8: its unscaled Hessian eigenvalues differ from V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, and it does not test ranking of training–test error gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors also conclude that their third-order SDE approximates discrete SAM more accurately than the previous second-order model. They attribute Eigen-SAM's improvements to more effective eigenvalue regularization; the reported spectrum and accuracy comparisons do not establish V7's specific correlation.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies sharpness-aware minimization and proposes Eigen-SAM, which adds an estimated top Hessian eigenvector component to the perturbation. It does not reproduce the listed studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The alignment and sharpness results are discussed for SAM; the test-accuracy comparisons vary dataset, architecture, training method, and—in fine-tuning—step budget. Eigen-SAM sensitivity to α is reported on ResNet-18/CIFAR-100, with a peak at α = 0.2; larger p values are also compared in Appendix F.

fits_no_version.finding: Eigen-SAM has higher mean test accuracy than SAM in all 14 architecture–dataset comparisons, by 0.1–0.9 percentage points. For ResNet-18/CIFAR-100, its final Hessian spectrum also has a smaller top eigenvalue and trace.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explicit eigenvector alignment can improve SAM's test performance; in one tested setting the improvement accompanies lower unscaled Hessian sharpness.

fits_no_version.finding: For a six-layer CNN on CIFAR-10, SAM's perturbation aligns poorly with the top Hessian eigenvector, and the authors report inefficient reduction of the top eigenvalue.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Practical SAM training need not satisfy the alignment assumptions used to explain its implicit eigenvalue regularization.

record.peer_reviewed: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
record.problems: The evidence on the claim is indirect: the paper does not measure training-test error gaps across models or use magnitude-aware sharpness. The Hessian spectrum comparison is qualitative in the text. Experiments use three independent repeats; SGD and SAM/Eigen-SAM have different training budgets in the stated comparisons (SGD gets twice as many epochs or steps).
record.rows_left_out: No rows left out; all individually tabulated test-accuracy results are recorded. Figure 3(a)'s α sensitivity and Appendix F's p sweep concern Eigen-SAM hyperparameter performance rather than a listed claim version; the α result is mentioned in method_sensitivity and the paper text, but no row is included because it compares the study's proposed method's setting rather than a claim version's object.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and paired natural-label versus random-label held-out performance.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the role of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a penalty.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with training–test error gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: SAM and Eigen-SAM use SGD as their base optimizer, so their comparison does not test V4. Comparing ResNet variants with WideResNet is not a controlled width sweep testing V2. Theorem 3.1 bounds population loss using empirical loss, an unscaled top eigenvalue, and additional terms under stated assumptions; it does not establish V7's magnitude-aware empirical ranking. Reported ± values are 95% confidence intervals from three repeats; higher means alone do not establish significance for every comparison.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
No width sweep around the zero-training-error threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.

The study measures top Hessian eigenvalue and reports a qualitative relationship with test accuracy, but does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or compare gaps among networks trained to similarly low training loss.

rows.subject: ResNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Compared Hessian spectrum after SAM and Eigen-SAM training.
rows.baseline: SAM spectrum; numerical values not stated
rows.value: Eigen-SAM has a smaller top eigenvalue and trace, with more eigenvalues concentrated near zero
rows.note: Authors say this observation aligns with their motivation and explains why Eigen-SAM generalizes better; no numerical spectrum values are given.
rows.check: The qualitative spectrum comparison is accurately reported, but observed is not a valid state relative to V7: unscaled eigenvalue and trace do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or gap rankings.

rows.subject: 6-layer SimpleCNN
rows.operation_detail: Tracked perturbation-vector alignment with the top Hessian eigenvector and the top eigenvalue.
rows.measure: Alignment and top Hessian eigenvalue over training
rows.value: Alignment was poor during training; SAM was unable to efficiently minimize the top eigenvalue when alignment was weak
rows.uncertainty: 95% confidence interval shown for alignment; numeric values not stated
rows.note: The paper describes the trend but gives no numeric values in the text.
rows.check: Poor perturbation–eigenvector alignment concerns SAM's optimization dynamics. It cannot establish even partial occurrence of any listed version.
